meta.titre: Cell Organelles: Structure, Function and Self-Replication

sections.contenu_markdown: At a fruit and vegetable market in Buea, a trader notices that ripe fruits are brightly coloured while the leaves are green. The difference lies inside the cells, in small structures called organelles. Each organelle has its own shape, its own membrane arrangement and its own job, and the GCE paper regularly asks you to match structure to function. Knowing which organelles have two membranes, which contain DNA and which make or move proteins will earn you easy marks.

items: Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, whereas prokaryotic cells do not.
The electron microscope has a higher resolution than the light microscope.
Aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose and makes ATP.

sections.titre: Organelles of eukaryotic cells: structure and function
sections.contenu_markdown:
An **organelle** is a specialised structure inside a cell that carries out one particular job. In eukaryotic cells the electron microscope shows the organelles in the table below.

| Organelle | Membrane | Key features | Main function |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nucleus | Double (nuclear envelope with pores) | Chromatin, nucleolus | Stores DNA, controls the cell, makes mRNA; nucleolus makes ribosomal subunits |
| Mitochondrion | Double; inner membrane folded into cristae | Matrix with 70S ribosomes and a loop of DNA | Aerobic respiration, making ATP |
| Chloroplast | Double; thylakoids stacked as grana in the stroma | Chlorophyll, 70S ribosomes, loop of DNA, starch grains | Photosynthesis |
| Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) | Single | 80S ribosomes on the surface | Makes, folds and transports proteins |
| Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) | Single | No ribosomes | Makes lipids and steroids, detoxifies |
| Golgi apparatus | Single (stack of flattened cisternae) | Vesicles bud from the edges | Modifies and packages proteins, forms lysosomes |
| Lysosome | Single | Hydrolytic enzymes | Digests worn-out organelles and engulfed material |
| Ribosome | None | 80S in the cytoplasm, 70S in mitochondria and chloroplasts | Translation, joining amino acids into polypeptides |
| Centriole (animal cells) | None | Nine triplets of microtubules | Forms the spindle during cell division |

Only three structures in the table have a **double membrane**: the nucleus, the mitochondrion and the chloroplast. All the others have a single membrane or none.

**Self-replication.** Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes. They make some of their own proteins and divide by binary fission, so they can increase in number independently of the nucleus, which divides only as part of mitosis. This is why they are described as semi-autonomous, and it supports the idea that they evolved from engulfed prokaryotes.

**Colour in plants.** Bright colours come from pigments in two different places: carotenoids (yellow, orange, red) stored in **chromoplasts**, and water-soluble anthocyanins (red, purple, blue) dissolved in the sap of the **vacuole**.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks about colour, storage or non-green parts of a plant
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Plastids are double-membrane organelles of plant cells that all develop from the same precursors.

- **Chloroplasts** contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
- **Chromoplasts** contain carotenoid pigments and give colour to ripe fruits, carrots and many petals.
- **Leucoplasts** are colourless and store food; **amyloplasts** store starch, for example in a cassava root or a potato tuber.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a cell makes a protein that leaves the cell, such as an enzyme or a hormone
variantes.contenu_markdown: Genetic information in the nucleus is copied as mRNA, which leaves through a nuclear pore. Ribosomes on the **RER** make the protein, which enters the lumen of the RER and folds. Transport vesicles bud off and carry it to the **Golgi apparatus**, where it is modified and packaged into secretory vesicles. These move to the cell surface membrane and release the protein by **exocytosis**. Mitochondria supply the ATP for the whole process.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must calculate sizes or explain why an organelle cannot be seen
variantes.contenu_markdown: Magnification $=\dfrac{\text{image size}}{\text{actual size}}$, so actual size $=\dfrac{\text{image size}}{\text{magnification}}$. Both sizes must be in the same unit before dividing: $1\ \mathrm{mm}=1000\ \mu\mathrm{m}$. The electron microscope has a much higher **resolution** than the light microscope, which is why ribosomes, cristae and membranes are seen only with it.

sections.enonce_markdown: An electron micrograph of a liver cell has a magnification of $\times12\,000$. On the micrograph an organelle with a double membrane and inner folds is $36\ \mathrm{mm}$ long. Identify the organelle and calculate its actual length in micrometres ($\mu\mathrm{m}$).

etapes.justification: A double membrane with the inner membrane folded into cristae is the signature of a mitochondrion; a chloroplast would show grana, and a liver cell has none.

etapes.action: Write the formula for actual size.
etapes.justification: Magnification is image size divided by actual size, so the actual size is the image size divided by the magnification.

etapes.action: Convert the image length to micrometres.
etapes.justification: Both sizes must be in the same unit; there are $1000\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ in $1\ \mathrm{mm}$.
This removes the enlargement and gives the real length.

etapes.action: Check that the answer is sensible.
etapes.justification: Mitochondria are typically between about $1$ and $10\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ long, so $3\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ is realistic.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The organelle is a mitochondrion and its actual length is **$3\ \mu\mathrm{m}$**.

items.erreur_markdown: Mitochondria make energy for the cell.
items.pourquoi_faux: Energy cannot be made. Mitochondria transfer the chemical energy of respiratory substrates into the chemical energy of ATP, which is the form the cell can use directly.
items.correction_markdown: Say that mitochondria **release energy from respiratory substrates to make ATP** by aerobic respiration.

items.erreur_markdown: Plant cells have chloroplasts instead of mitochondria.
items.pourquoi_faux: Chloroplasts make carbohydrates in light, while mitochondria release energy from them. A leaf cell respires day and night, and root cells have no chloroplasts at all but still need ATP.
items.correction_markdown: Plant cells that photosynthesise contain **both** chloroplasts and mitochondria.

items.erreur_markdown: Lysosomes, the Golgi apparatus and vacuoles all have double membranes.
items.pourquoi_faux: Only the nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplasts (with other plastids) are surrounded by two membranes. Lysosomes, the Golgi apparatus, the ER and the vacuole each have a single membrane.
items.correction_markdown: Learn the list: **nucleus, mitochondrion, chloroplast** have a double membrane; the rest have one or none.

items.erreur_markdown: Ribosomes are found only on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
items.pourquoi_faux: Many ribosomes lie free in the cytoplasm and make proteins used inside the cell. Ribosomes also occur inside mitochondria and chloroplasts, where they are the smaller 70S type, and they have no membrane.
items.correction_markdown: Ribosomes are **membrane-free**; they are free or attached to the RER, and 70S ribosomes occur in mitochondria and chloroplasts.

items.erreur_markdown: All bright colours in a flower come from chromoplasts.
items.pourquoi_faux: Carotenoids in chromoplasts give yellow, orange and some red colours, but red, purple and blue petals are often coloured by anthocyanin dissolved in the vacuolar sap, which is not an organelle with a double membrane.
items.correction_markdown: State which pigment is involved: **carotenoids in chromoplasts** or **anthocyanin in the vacuole**.

items.enonce_markdown:
Name the organelle described in each case.

(a) The main site of ATP production by aerobic respiration.
(b) A stack of flattened sacs that modifies proteins and packages them into vesicles.
(c) A single-membrane sac containing hydrolytic enzymes that digests worn-out cell parts.
(d) A structure with no membrane where amino acids are joined into polypeptides.
(e) A pair of structures in an animal cell made of microtubules that organise the spindle.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Mitochondrion**, whose cristae and matrix carry the enzymes of aerobic respiration.

(b) **Golgi apparatus**, a stack of cisternae from which vesicles bud.

(c) **Lysosome**, which holds hydrolytic enzymes.

(d) **Ribosome**, the site of translation.

(e) **Centrioles**, which form the spindle at cell division.

items.enonce_markdown:
A student studies two electron micrographs.

(a) In the first, a chloroplast is $60\ \mathrm{mm}$ long and the magnification is $\times7\,500$. Calculate its actual length in $\mu\mathrm{m}$.
(b) In the second, a mitochondrion known to be $2\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ long measures $50\ \mathrm{mm}$ on the image. Calculate the magnification.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Convert the image length: $60\ \mathrm{mm}=60\,000\ \mu\mathrm{m}$.

Actual size $=\dfrac{60\,000}{7\,500}=$ **$8\ \mu\mathrm{m}$**.

(b) Convert the image length: $50\ \mathrm{mm}=50\,000\ \mu\mathrm{m}$.

Magnification $=\dfrac{\text{image size}}{\text{actual size}}=\dfrac{50\,000}{2}=$ **$\times25\,000$**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A cell lining the pancreas makes a digestive enzyme and releases it into a duct. Its electron micrograph shows a large nucleus, a very extensive rough endoplasmic reticulum, a prominent Golgi apparatus, many vesicles near the cell surface and many mitochondria.

(a) Describe, in order, the path taken by the enzyme from the gene that codes for it to its release from the cell.
(b) Explain why the cell contains so many mitochondria.
(c) Explain why the cell surface membrane increases in area as the enzyme is released.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The gene in the **nucleus** is transcribed into mRNA, which leaves through a **nuclear pore**. Ribosomes on the **rough ER** translate it, and the polypeptide enters the lumen of the ER where it folds. **Transport vesicles** carry it to the **Golgi apparatus**, where it is modified and packaged in **secretory vesicles**. These move to the cell surface membrane and release the enzyme by **exocytosis**.

(b) Making, moving and packaging proteins, and moving vesicles, all need ATP. Many mitochondria provide a large supply of ATP by aerobic respiration.

(c) Each secretory vesicle fuses with the cell surface membrane during exocytosis, so the vesicle membrane becomes part of the surface membrane and the area increases.

items_markdown: Three organelles have a **double membrane**: the nucleus, the mitochondrion and the chloroplast (and other plastids).
Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain **circular DNA and 70S ribosomes** and divide by binary fission, so they self-replicate.
RER makes and folds proteins; the Golgi apparatus modifies and packages them; secretory vesicles release them by exocytosis.
Bright plant colours come from **carotenoids in chromoplasts** or **anthocyanin in the vacuole**.
Actual size = image size divided by magnification, after converting to the same unit ($1\ \mathrm{mm}=1000\ \mu\mathrm{m}$).
